correctness.rationale: The incidence graph has 20 degree-four vertices and 40 edges. Tie retention is equivalent to majority of the four neighbors and the vertex's own bit. Independently constructing the transition on all 2^20 states, then testing the first F^(t+2)(x)=F^t(x) through t=7, reproduces all twelve nonzero first-entry/period cells and leaves no unclassified state. Testing F^(t+1)(x)=F^t(x) at entry separates fixed and primitive period-two states, yielding 4,036 fixed states, 702 period-two states (351 temporal orbits), and basin totals of 959,624 and 88,952. The time-seven row has 960 members, split 480/480 between the two unanimous equilibria. A separate pullback of the all-zero state using update masks for the two bipartition classes gives exactly 960 first hits at time six and 480 at time seven; global complementation proves identical counts for all-one. These exhaust the two late fixed-basin rows. The five doubled pairs are precisely the non-singleton identical-open-neighborhood classes. Each permutation of those pairs forces the edge-vertex permutation, and arbitrary internal twin swaps are allowed. Thus the nine natural generators give the full group of order 3840. Its orbit traversal, including a temporal phase swap only among period-two states, yields the exact 44/8 class counts and both stated size histograms.
residual_risks: The exhaustive verification concerns the specified fixed graph, fully synchronous update, and current-opinion tie rule only. It does not imply seven-step convergence or unanimity for other regular graphs.

evidence: The general majority theorem bounds first two-periodic entry after reducing twin families. On Folkman the asymmetric graph retains all twenty vertices and forty edges, all vertices even, giving 1+min(40,20+5+35)=41. The comparator's exact same-graph finding additionally enumerates 26 individual-attractor basin sizes, including 207,670 at each unanimous attractor.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theorem handles the right rule, but its upper bound does not imply sharp time seven or any exact state counts. The broader exact same-graph comparator, not the general convergence bound, is what establishes overlap.
